clinician.final_diagnosis: Acute longitudinal extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) secondary to COVID-19
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with a 1-day history of acute onset sharp right-sided back pain lateral to the thoracic spine at T8, accompanied by progressive bilateral leg numbness and paresthesia, urinary retention, constipation, and impaired gait. She had tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 on RT-PCR 5 days prior to admission. Neurological examination revealed bilaterally exaggerated knee reflexes and positive Babinski's sign (upper motor neuron signs) with grade 2 motor weakness in ankle dorsiflexion, great toe extension, and ankle plantar flexion, and sensory impairment at L4-L5 with absent sensation at S1-S2 dermatomes (lower motor neuron signs). MRI of the spine with gadolinium enhancement showed T2-weighted hyperintense lesions in the thoracic region of the spinal cord with multiple regions of patchy hyperintensity seen both centrally and peripherally, consistent with transverse myelitis. The subarachnoid space was normal and the lumbosacral region was normal, ruling out cauda equina syndrome. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed elevated protein at 0.4 g with minimal cellularity (<0.001×10⁹/L white blood cells) and no organisms, consistent with a demyelinating process. Brain MRI was largely unremarkable with only tiny frontal-parietal high signals. The patient was treated with methylprednisolone 1 g intravenously once daily for 3 days, followed by oral prednisolone 60 mg daily with omeprazole gastroprotection. During the course of steroid therapy over a 2-week admission, she demonstrated excellent clinical response with full recovery of sensation in dermatomes L4, L5, S1, and S2, regained motor function in her lower limbs, achieved independent ambulation and stair climbing with crutches, and fully regained bladder function.
